location: Published p. 111 (PDF p. 4), Introduction; p. 117 (PDF p. 10), Results and Table 1; p. 122 (PDF p. 15), General discussion
quote: Second, the initial phase of our study did not include a control condition.
reason: Although the prior main review accepted β1 = .28 from the published private-archive PDF/TXT (p. 117, Table 1), that parameter is a within-participant initial-phase piecewise LGCM growth slope across all trained participants rather than the requested course-versus-control comparison. Because the replication provided the initial intervention to all participants without an untreated control group (only comparing 'how' vs. 'why' booster sessions in the later maintenance phase), the target contrast is absent and unmappable.

location: Published p. 111 (PDF p. 4), Introduction; p. 113 (PDF p. 6), Method - Participants; p. 122 (PDF p. 15), General discussion
quote: Second, the initial phase of our study did not include a control condition.
reason: The prior main review matched N = 141 (p. 113), which is the total retained single-arm intervention cohort in the published private-archive copy, but all retained participants received the initial course. Because no untreated control group exists in the replication to form the requested course-versus-control self-efficacy contrast, the analytic sample size for the target comparison is undeterminable.

location: Published p. 120 (PDF p. 13), General discussion; p. 122 (PDF p. 15), General discussion
quote: Second, the initial phase of our study did not include a control condition.
reason: While the prior main review noted that the authors describe the initial intervention as effective on psychological outcomes including self-efficacy (p. 120) in the published private-archive copy, that narrative evaluates within-participant initial-phase improvement across all trained patients and explicitly notes that outcomes cannot be compared against a no-intervention control group. Consequently, no effect-specific narrative verdict can be confirmed for the requested course-versus-control self-efficacy contrast.
